text:
andrew: FYI — Acme procurement just sent back the Order Form with two blockers: they want Net45 and their procurement portal is rejecting DocuSign envelopes from our account. Also they attached an MSA redline asking to raise the SLA to 99.95% and prefer liquidated damages instead of service credits. Can procurement/legal weigh in?
sara: Thanks — can you drop the redline PDF here? Quick instincts: we generally don't accept LDs for hosted services; we offer service credits capped at monthly fees. 99.95% is a pretty big change vs our standard 99.9; we can negotiate but need clear uptime/window and credit calculation. Also need to validate DPA changes.
kevin: From finance: Net45 is non-standard but possible for strategic deals with completed vendor setup + credit check. We will need a signed Order Form + PO or a countersigned PO in their portal, plus W-9 and vendor onboarding form. If they insist on PO-first, that must be a fully executed PO referencing our Order Form.
sam: Procurement portal detail: their vendor ID lookup fails if the signer email domain doesn't match the legal entity on the contract. Their system blocks DocuSign automated senders like `redwood-inference-ds@docusign.net`. Workarounds we've used: 1) provide a fully-signed PDF (wet or DocuSign) from our side and they manually upload it; 2) they sign the PO in their portal and attach our signed Order Form; or 3) we provide a vendor alias that matches their portal. Which is feasible?
elaine: Can legal accept language that explicitly allows a Customer Purchase Order to act as acceptance? Eg: `Buyer’s issuance of a Purchase Order that references the Order Form shall constitute acceptance of the Order Form by Buyer and be binding.` That usually lets procurement accept our signed Order Form plus their PO. Sara?
sara: That clause is OK if we add a carveout: PO acceptance only for non-substantive changes and provided the PO references the Order Form ID. We can't let a PO alter pricing/SLA silently. I'll draft a short clause: 1) PO = acceptance if references Order Form ID; 2) any conflicting terms in a PO are void unless explicitly agreed.
andrew: Also re: their SLA ask — they want LD instead of credits. We should be firm: capped service credits only, with definition and measurement window. Can we quantify the cap at monthly recurring fees?
sara: Correct — we push for service credits, cap = monthly fees for the affected service, with a 30-day cure period for incidents. I will prepare redline language replacing an LD ask.
contract-bot: Upload complete: `Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf` available at /files/1912345678/Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf
kevin: Timeline note: Finance needs completed vendor setup to process Net45. That includes: W-9, tax ID, banking info for EFT (if they prefer), and a signed Order Form + PO. If they can't provide banking details, we fallback to wire/EFT with origination fees on them.
sam: Acme says procurement cycle runs Friday EOD. They asked if we can accept a signed Order Form + emailed PO (pdf) and then they'll complete portal upload later. That would be a yes from them but we need legal/finance signoff.
elaine: If legal signs the clause that a PO referencing the Order Form is acceptance, we can accept emailed PO + signed Order Form to meet their cycle, then complete vendor onboarding after. Finance: OK?
kevin: OK but subject to receiving vendor docs within 5 business days or Net45 hold. I'll send them the vendor setup form now.
andrew: Plan I will propose to Acme in the reply: 1) We accept their emailed PO referencing Order Form ID + our signed Order Form as immediate acceptance for procurement cycle; 2) We will not accept LDs, will offer service-credit language with cap at monthly fees (legal will post redline); 3) Finance to provide vendor setup link for Net45 — they must complete by next Wed. @sara please post the redline by Thursday 10am so I can share with them.
sara: On it. I'll post the redline here with tracked changes and a short plain-English summary. :thumbsup:
andrew: Great — I'll draft the customer-facing reply and loop Acme. Thanks all. :pray:
